title: Digital specialist referral intake
description: Allow a primary-care referral coordinator to submit a complete specialist referral with patient consent, clinical reason, preferred specialty, and supporting documents.
user_goal: Submit a complete referral without rekeying patient details.
business_value: Reduce incomplete referrals and give every downstream team a traceable starting record.
acceptance_criteria: Given an authenticated coordinator with access to the patient's care organization; when they submit a referral containing consent status patient identifiers receiving specialty clinical reason and at least one contact method; then the system creates one immutable referral record returns a reference number and shows the referral as Awaiting clinical review. Given missing required information or an invalid consent status; when submission is attempted; then no referral is created and each correctable field is identified. Given the same idempotency key is submitted again; when the original request was accepted; then the original referral is returned without creating a duplicate.
dependencies: Patient identity service; organization authorization; document storage; audit ledger
non_functional_requirements: Server-side organization and role authorization; consent and patient identifiers excluded from application logs; encrypted document storage; WCAG 2.2 AA; keyboard-operable form; p95 accepted submission under 3 seconds; immutable audit event for create and validation failure.
out_of_scope: Referral scheduling; payer authorization determination; clinical triage policy authoring.
success_metric: Complete referral submission rate; incomplete-referral correction rate; duplicate referral rate.

title: Clinical documentation request and reconciliation
description: Allow the receiving specialty team to request missing clinical documents and reconcile received documents against a referral before it is ready for review.
user_goal: Request and track only the records needed to make the referral clinically reviewable.
business_value: Shorten time to a reviewable referral while preserving a minimum-necessary and auditable document trail.
acceptance_criteria: Given a referral in Awaiting clinical review; when an authorized specialty coordinator marks a required document as missing and sends a request; then the requester recipient document type due date and referral version are retained and the referral shows Needs information. Given an authorized source uploads a document for an open request; when file type size malware scan and patient-to-referral match succeed; then the document is versioned linked to the request and the referral shows Ready for specialist review only after every required request is satisfied. Given a document does not match the referral patient or fails safety validation; when upload is attempted; then it is quarantined no clinical reviewer can access it and an audit event records the rejection reason.
dependencies: CH-1001; document storage; malware scanning service; patient identity service; notification service
non_functional_requirements: Minimum-necessary document metadata; encrypted transit and storage; server-side patient and organization match; immutable version history; antivirus result required before availability; p95 document-status update under 5 seconds; WCAG 2.2 AA.
out_of_scope: Clinical diagnosis; specialist scheduling; external EHR write-back; automated clinical decision making.
success_metric: Median time from referral creation to review-ready; document reconciliation success rate; quarantined-upload rate; unauthorized document-access rate equals zero.

title: Referral decision communication and next-step coordination
description: Allow a specialist reviewer to record an accountable referral decision and give the patient and referring practice clear, appropriate next steps.
user_goal: Record a referral decision with clinically appropriate next steps and notify the people who need to act.
business_value: Close the referral loop, reduce patient uncertainty, and create an auditable handoff to scheduling or follow-up care.
acceptance_criteria: Given a referral is Ready for specialist review and the reviewer is authorized for the receiving organization; when the reviewer records Accepted Needs more information or Not appropriate with a permitted rationale and next-step instruction; then the decision is bound to the reviewed referral and document versions, an immutable audit event is retained, and the referral state changes once. Given Accepted is recorded; when patient communication preference permits notification; then the patient and referring practice receive a notification that contains no sensitive clinical detail and directs them to the authenticated portal for next steps. Given a reviewer tries to decide their own submitted referral or a stale referral version; when the decision is submitted; then no decision is recorded and the user receives a clear conflict or refresh instruction.
dependencies: CH-1001; CH-1002; reviewer authorization; notification service; patient portal; audit ledger
non_functional_requirements: Separation of duties between referral submitter and decision reviewer; server-side version check; minimum-necessary notifications; immutable decision record; WCAG 2.2 AA; accessible notification status; p95 decision save under 2 seconds; delivery and notification failures monitored.
out_of_scope: Appointment scheduling; emergency triage; clinical treatment recommendations; automated denial decisions.
success_metric: Referral-loop closure rate; median decision time after review readiness; patient notification delivery rate; stale-decision rejection rate.
